description: Advanced SQL — CTEs, window functions, subqueries, complex logic

cases.natural_language: Show me the running total of monthly revenue
cases.expected_sql: WITH monthly_revenue AS (SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', o.order_date) AS month, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.id = oi.order_id GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', o.order_date)) SELECT month, revenue, SUM(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS running_total FROM monthly_revenue ORDER BY month
cases.description: CTE with window function for running total

cases.natural_language: Rank customers by total spending and show top 5
cases.expected_sql: WITH customer_spending AS (SELECT c.id, c.name, SUM(o.total) AS total_spent, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(o.total) DESC) AS spending_rank FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.id, c.name) SELECT name, total_spent, spending_rank FROM customer_spending WHERE spending_rank <= 5
cases.description: CTE with RANK window function and filter

cases.expected_sql: WITH monthly AS (SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date) AS month, SUM(total) AS revenue FROM orders GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date)) SELECT month, revenue, LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS prev_revenue, ROUND((revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month)) * 100.0 / LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month), 2) AS growth_pct FROM monthly ORDER BY month
cases.description: LAG window function for period-over-period comparison

cases.natural_language: Find products that are priced above the average in their category
cases.expected_sql: SELECT p.name, p.price, p.category FROM products p WHERE p.price > (SELECT AVG(p2.price) FROM products p2 WHERE p2.category = p.category)
cases.description: Correlated subquery comparing against category average

cases.natural_language: Show customer segments: classify customers as High, Medium, or Low value based on their total spending compared to the average
cases.expected_sql: WITH customer_totals AS (SELECT c.id, c.name, SUM(o.total) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.id, c.name), stats AS (SELECT AVG(total_spent) AS avg_spent, STDDEV(total_spent) AS std_spent FROM customer_totals) SELECT ct.name, ct.total_spent, CASE WHEN ct.total_spent > s.avg_spent + s.std_spent THEN 'High Value' WHEN ct.total_spent > s.avg_spent - s.std_spent THEN 'Medium Value' ELSE 'Low Value' END AS segment FROM customer_totals ct CROSS JOIN stats s ORDER BY ct.total_spent DESC
